display_name: Nila Valley Scholar of the Kerala School
one_line: A household-based astronomer-mathematician from the scholar lineages of the Nila valley, preserving and teaching science in medieval Kerala.

appearance.age_look: mid-30s, lean and slightly wiry, with the calm posture of a teacher used to long hours of study and recitation
appearance.face: oval face with medium-brown Kerala complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed black moustache, soft but focused dark eyes, a small tilaka of sandal paste on the forehead, default expression gentle and attentive as if mid-explanation
appearance.hair: glossy black hair oiled and drawn back into a short, tidy knot at the back of the head, front kept smooth without loose bangs; wears a thin white cotton headband tied low around the crown, echoing a simple ritual band
appearance.costume: traditional Namboothiri-style attire: an unstitched off-white cotton uttariya (upper cloth) wrapped around the torso and over the left shoulder like a shawl, covering the chest modestly, paired with a matching off-white cotton dhoti worn ankle-length and pleated in front, bordered with a narrow golden-yellow zari edge; the cloth is plain but finely woven, draping cleanly; a simple tulasi bead mala around the neck, a thin gold bangle on the right wrist, and a waist cord visible where the uttariya shifts; he is barefoot, as in temple and household study spaces, but feet are clean and well-kept
appearance.signature: a neatly bundled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cotton string, with one leaf slightly fanned out to show inscribed Sanskrit numerals and syllables, held in his left hand while his right hand gestures in teaching

ref_desc: A lean, mid-30s Nila valley scholar with an oval medium-brown face, oiled black hair in a back knot and white headband, wearing off-white dhoti and uttariya with golden-yellow border, simple beads and bangle, holding a red-tied palm-leaf manuscript in a warm off-white, gold, brown, black and soft red palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a medieval Kerala Nila valley scholar-mathematician: a lean man in his mid-30s with an oval medium-brown face, dark attentive eyes, straight nose, and a neat black moustache, bearing a small sandalwood tilaka on his forehead. His glossy black hair is oiled and pulled into a short knot at the back of his head, front smooth without bangs, with a thin white cotton headband tied around the crown. He wears traditional Namboothiri-style clothing: an off-white cotton dhoti, ankle-length and carefully pleated in front with a narrow golden-yellow zari border, and an off-white cotton uttariya upper cloth draped securely around his torso and over the left shoulder, modestly covering his chest like a shawl. Add a simple tulasi bead mala at his neck, a thin gold bangle on his right wrist, and a waist cord hinted at where the uttariya shifts; keep him barefoot, with clean, well-drawn feet. In his left hand he carries a neatly bundled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cotton string, one leaf slightly fanned open to suggest inscribed Sanskrit numerals and syllables, while his right hand is posed in a gentle teaching gesture. Use a restrained palette of off-white for garments, golden yellow for borders, warm brown for skin, black for hair and eyes, and soft red for the manuscript tie, showing front, side, and back views to make the face, hair knot, draped costume, and palm-leaf manuscript clearly repeatable.
